statement: Roughly how many seconds are there in a year?

choices.misconception: I converted the year into minutes, 365 x 24 x 60, and stopped one step short of seconds.
I used 360 seconds in an hour instead of 3600.
I used 3650 days in a year, slipping a factor of ten into the day count.
I multiplied by 60 one time too many, as though there were another sixty-step unit below the second.

hints: Build the answer one conversion at a time.
Go from a year to days, days to hours, hours to minutes and minutes to seconds, checking after each step that the size of the number has grown by about the right factor.
365 x 24 is about 8800 hours, times 3600 seconds in an hour.

solutions.reliable: A year is about 365 x 24 = 8760 hours, and each hour holds 3600 seconds, giving roughly 31.5 million. The transferable idea: estimate one conversion at a time and sanity-check the order of magnitude after each, because a single missed factor of sixty moves the answer by a whole choice.
solutions.elegant: A useful fact worth carrying: a year is close to pi times ten million seconds.

whyOnTest: Order-of-magnitude questions are won by the student who tracks powers of ten, and every distractor here is one conversion away from right.
author: Devansh Sanghavi
